_about: Every load the rifle set uses. muzzleFps is the speed from the barrel the rifle in this set actually has; where the maker measured in a different barrel the figure is an estimate by the rule stated. bc is the ballistic coefficient the engine uses with dragModel (G1 or G7); where the maker publishes both, the one the maker's own trajectory table follows is used. spreadMoa is the five-shot extreme spread in minutes of angle (MOA, 1/60 of a degree, about 1.047 inches at 100 yards) expected from that rifle and load.

source.note: retailer listing of the IMI load; no IMI page could be found by search. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches

Shooting Illustrated: "advertised 3,166 fps from a 20-inch barrel"; the review measured 3,080 fps from a 16.25-inch barrel at 21 F. IMI publishes no page this session could find. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches
the advertised figure's barrel. read from the search engine's indexed text of this page on the date given: this session's network allowed web search but no page fetches

muzzleFps.estimate: 3,166 fps from 20 in, adjusted from the maker's test barrel by 25 feet per second per inch of barrel, the usual rule of thumb for 5.56 (Gorilla Ammunition lists its 69 gr Sierra load at 2,900 fps from 24 in and 2,630 fps from 16 in, 34 fps per inch, https://www.gorillaammo.com/?p=224; the standard 25 fps per inch is used), for the 16-inch barrel in this set

bc.estimate: IMI publishes no ballistic coefficient. 0.243 G1 is the figure listed for Hornady's 55 gr full metal jacket boat tail bullet (#2267), a bullet of the same weight and shape, on retailer pages quoting Hornady (https://x-reload.com/hrn-2267.html, https://recreationid.com/hornady/traditional-fmj-22-55-g-rifle-bullets-mpn-2267.html, read 2026-11-16)

spreadMoa.estimate: ball ammunition from a 16-inch carbine; makers publish no group size. Match loads are set tighter than ball and surplus
